UI_EHR_Codex_painkiller_addiction_Incuba: Si sviluppa dopo un uso prolungato o eccessivo di antidolorifici.
UI_EHR_Codex_painkiller_addiction_Durati: Persistente. Lo stadio 3 non guarisce spontaneamente.
UI_EHR_Codex_painkiller_addiction_Cause: Uso ripetuto di antidolorifici normali o artigianali, soprattutto cinque o più dosi in 24 ore o assunzioni troppo ravvicinate.
UI_EHR_Codex_painkiller_addiction_Sympto: Desiderio compulsivo, stress e depressione persistenti, sete aumentata. Una dose attiva di antidolorifico o buprenorfina sopprime temporaneamente i sintomi di astinenza.
UI_EHR_Codex_painkiller_addiction_Preven: Evita dosi troppo frequenti e mantieni l'uso giornaliero di antidolorifici sotto la fascia ad alto rischio.
UI_EHR_Codex_painkiller_addiction_Treatm: La buprenorfina cura la condizione in 120 ore: 10 dosi, una ogni 12 ore. Ogni dose attiva sopprime i sintomi di astinenza.

UI_EHR_Text_YouTakePainkillersThePainBeg: Prendi degli antidolorifici. Il dolore comincia ad attenuarsi.
UI_EHR_Text_YouTakeAntidepressantsTheEdg: Prendi degli antidepressivi. La tensione si attenua un po'.
UI_EHR_Text_YouDrinkTheHerbalTeaWarmthSe: Bevi la tisana. Un tepore si diffonde nel petto.
UI_EHR_Text_YouDrinkTheAntipyreticTeaThe: Bevi la tisana antipiretica. La febbre comincia a calare.
UI_EHR_Text_YouDrinkTheHomemadeCoughSyru: Bevi lo sciroppo per la tosse artigianale. La tosse si placa.
UI_EHR_Text_YouTakeTheHomemadeMuscleRela: Prendi il miorilassante artigianale. I crampi si attenuano.
UI_EHR_Text_YouTakeHomemadePainkillersTh: Prendi antidolorifici artigianali. Il dolore comincia ad attenuarsi.
UI_EHR_Text_YouTakeHomemadeSleepingPills: Prendi sonniferi artigianali. La sonnolenza comincia a farsi sentire.
UI_EHR_Text_YouDrinkTheRelaxantTeaYourNe: Bevi la tisana rilassante. I nervi cominciano a distendersi.
UI_EHR_Text_YouTakeCombatStimulantsEvery: Prendi stimolanti da combattimento. Tutto diventa subito più nitido.
UI_EHR_Text_YouApplyHomemadeAntisepticCr: Applichi la crema antisettica artigianale sulla ferita.
UI_EHR_Text_YouSwallowHomemadeActivatedC: Ingerisci carbone attivo artigianale. Assorbe le tossine.
UI_EHR_Text_YouApplyHomemadeTopicalPerme: Applichi la permetrina topica artigianale. Gli acari dovrebbero cominciare a morire.
UI_EHR_Text_YouActivateTheWarmingPackAnd: Attivi lo scaldino e lo tieni vicino al corpo.
UI_EHR_Text_YouTakeTheDualOrexinReceptor: Prendi il farmaco antagonista dei due recettori dell'orexina. Dormire sembra di nuovo possibile.
UI_EHR_Text_YouTakeBuprenorphineTheWithd: Prendi la buprenorfina. L'astinenza comincia a calmarsi.
UI_EHR_Text_YouApplyHomemadeAntibioticOi: Applichi la pomata antibiotica artigianale sulla zona infetta.
UI_EHR_Text_YouTriggerTheAutoInjectorAdr: Azioni l'autoiniettore. L'adrenalina invade il tuo organismo.

UI_profdesc_EHRDoctor: Un medico addestrato in EHR. Inizia con un pronto soccorso avanzato, abilità di base con la lama corta e conoscenza completa delle malattie.
UI_profdesc_EHRSurgeon: Un chirurgo esperto. Inizia con il maestro Pronto Soccorso, abilità con la lama corta più forte, conoscenza completa delle malattie e Maestro del bisturi.

UI_EHR_Codex_LockedDesc: Leggi il volantino della malattia corrispondente o raggiungi il livello 8 di Pronto Soccorso per sbloccare sintomi, cause, prevenzione e note sul trattamento.
UI_EHR_Codex_food_poisoning_Symptoms: Nausea, vomito, perdita di resistenza, fame e sete aumentate.
UI_EHR_Codex_food_poisoning_Prevention: Mangia cibo fresco ed evita quello avariato, molto bruciato o stantio.
UI_EHR_Codex_food_poisoning_Treatment: Compresse antinausea, polvere di elettroliti e carbone attivo. Il carbone attivo può curarla nel tempo.
UI_EHR_Codex_gastroenteritis_Cause: Mangiare con mani sporche o insanguinate.
UI_EHR_Codex_gastroenteritis_Symptoms: Nausea grave, vomito, disidratazione, mal di stomaco e stanchezza.
UI_EHR_Codex_gastroenteritis_Prevention: Lava le mani prima di mangiare, preferibilmente con sapone e acqua pulita.
UI_EHR_Codex_gastroenteritis_Treatment: Antidiarroici, polvere di elettroliti, capsule antivirali o ciprofloxacina endovenosa nei casi batterici gravi.
UI_EHR_Codex_trichinosis_Cause: Selvaggina cruda o poco cotta e carne cruda non sicura.
UI_EHR_Codex_trichinosis_Symptoms: Dolore muscolare intenso, febbre, debolezza e pericolosa perdita di salute negli stadi gravi.
UI_EHR_Codex_trichinosis_Prevention: Cuoci bene la carne, soprattutto la selvaggina.
UI_EHR_Codex_trichinosis_Treatment: Miorilassanti e antinfiammatori per i sintomi; compresse antiparassitarie o iniezione di albendazolo per curare.
UI_EHR_Codex_toxin_poisoning_Cause: Bacche velenose, funghi velenosi o altri cibi tossici.
UI_EHR_Codex_toxin_poisoning_Symptoms: Nausea violenta, vomito, vertigini, vista offuscata, debolezza e pericoloso avvelenamento sistemico.
UI_EHR_Codex_toxin_poisoning_Prevention: Evita alimenti selvatici non identificati se non puoi verificarne la sicurezza.
UI_EHR_Codex_toxin_poisoning_Treatment: Il carbone attivo è il trattamento principale. Compresse antinausea ed elettroliti alleviano i sintomi.
UI_EHR_Codex_dysentery_Cause: Acqua contaminata o grave contaminazione gastrointestinale.
UI_EHR_Codex_dysentery_Symptoms: Diarrea grave, vomito, disidratazione, febbre, debolezza e possibile perdita di sangue.
UI_EHR_Codex_dysentery_Prevention: Bevi acqua pulita o bollita ed evita fonti d'acqua non sicure.
UI_EHR_Codex_dysentery_Treatment: Elettroliti e antidiarroici per i sintomi; ciprofloxacina endovenosa per le infezioni batteriche gravi.
UI_EHR_Codex_common_cold_Cause: Esposizione al freddo, all'umidità o prolungata mentre si è esausti.
UI_EHR_Codex_common_cold_Symptoms: Tosse, starnuti, febbre lieve, stanchezza e resistenza ridotta.
UI_EHR_Codex_common_cold_Prevention: Resta al caldo e all'asciutto, riposati e proteggiti dal maltempo.
UI_EHR_Codex_common_cold_Treatment: Riposo, liquidi, antitussivi e antipiretici contro la febbre; compresse per raffreddore e influenza o capsule antivirali possono curarla nel tempo.
UI_EHR_Codex_pneumonia_Cause: Malattia respiratoria grave o non trattata, esposizione al freddo o salute indebolita.
UI_EHR_Codex_pneumonia_Symptoms: Febbre, tosse, dolore toracico, perdita di resistenza e insufficienza respiratoria potenzialmente fatale.
UI_EHR_Codex_pneumonia_Prevention: Tratta presto le malattie respiratorie ed evita l'esposizione prolungata al freddo.
UI_EHR_Codex_pneumonia_Treatment: Gli antibiotici su prescrizione o ad ampio spettro curano nel tempo; la ciprofloxacina endovenosa è la cura clinica rapida. Il broncodilatatore aiuta la respirazione, gli antitussivi riducono la tosse e gli antipiretici abbassano la febbre.
UI_EHR_Codex_hypothermia_Cause: Temperatura corporea bassa dovuta a freddo, vestiti bagnati, vento o esposizione.
UI_EHR_Codex_hypothermia_Symptoms: Brividi, debolezza, confusione, stanchezza e pericoloso calo della temperatura.
UI_EHR_Codex_hypothermia_Prevention: Indossa vestiti isolanti, resta all'asciutto e riparati al chiuso durante il freddo intenso.
UI_EHR_Codex_hypothermia_Treatment: Riscaldati, indossa vestiti asciutti, riposa e usa fonti di calore esterne.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_exhaustion_Cause: Esposizione al caldo, disidratazione, vestiti pesanti o sforzi con clima caldo.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_exhaustion_Symptoms: Vertigini, nausea, debolezza, sete, stanchezza e surriscaldamento.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_exhaustion_Prevention: Idratati, riposa all'ombra, indossa abiti leggeri ed evita sforzi eccessivi al caldo.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_exhaustion_Treatment: Rinfrescati, riposa, bevi acqua e usa polvere di elettroliti.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_stroke_Incubation: Può svilupparsi da un esaurimento da calore non trattato.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_stroke_Duration: Critico finché la temperatura corporea non viene controllata.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_stroke_Cause: Esposizione a caldo estremo o grave disidratazione.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_stroke_Symptoms: Temperatura corporea estrema, delirio, confusione, vomito, collassi o svenimenti, disidratazione e perdita di salute potenzialmente fatale.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_stroke_Prevention: Evita il caldo estremo, idratati abbondantemente e tratta presto l'esaurimento da calore.
UI_EHR_Codex_heat_stroke_Treatment: Raffreddamento immediato. Le borse di ghiaccio istantaneo possono curare il colpo di calore con 4 applicazioni; liquidi ed elettroliti aiutano contro la disidratazione.
UI_EHR_Codex_corpse_sickness_Cause: Esposizione prolungata a cadaveri in decomposizione, soprattutto in spazi chiusi.
UI_EHR_Codex_corpse_sickness_Symptoms: Irritazione agli occhi, nausea, vertigini, debolezza, tosse e possibile collasso in caso di esposizione elevata.
UI_EHR_Codex_corpse_sickness_Prevention: Ventila gli spazi pieni di cadaveri e indossa una protezione facciale efficace.
UI_EHR_Codex_corpse_sickness_Treatment: Aria fresca immediatamente. Le compresse antinausea alleviano i sintomi; un kit di supporto respiratorio o corticosteroidi possono trattare i casi gravi.
UI_EHR_Codex_cadaveric_aspergillosis_Cau: Spore fungine da cadaveri in decomposizione in condizioni umide, bagnate o fredde.
UI_EHR_Codex_cadaveric_aspergillosis_Sym: Irritazione respiratoria, febbre, tosse, respiro sibilante, perdita di resistenza e debolezza.
UI_EHR_Codex_cadaveric_aspergillosis_Pre: Indossa una protezione facciale vicino a zone umide piene di cadaveri ed evita di respirare aria contaminata.
UI_EHR_Codex_cadaveric_aspergillosis_Tre: Inalatore broncodilatatore e antipiretici per i sintomi; compresse antimicotiche o amfotericina endovenosa per curare.
UI_EHR_Codex_tuberculosis_Cause: Esposizione respiratoria prolungata in ambienti contaminati con molti cadaveri.
UI_EHR_Codex_tuberculosis_Symptoms: Tosse persistente, febbre, stanchezza, perdita di peso, sudorazione notturna e sangue con la tosse nei casi gravi.
UI_EHR_Codex_tuberculosis_Prevention: Evita l'esposizione prolungata ai cadaveri e indossa una protezione respiratoria.
UI_EHR_Codex_tuberculosis_Treatment: Antibiotici antitubercolari o confezione combinata di rifampicina. Antitussivi e antipiretici riducono solo i sintomi.
UI_EHR_Codex_wound_infection_Cause: Ferite sporche, fasciature inadeguate o contaminazione delle ferite non trattata.
UI_EHR_Codex_wound_infection_Symptoms: Dolore, gonfiore, arrossamento, pus, febbre e peggioramento della ferita.
UI_EHR_Codex_wound_infection_Prevention: Pulisci le ferite, usa bende sterili e sostituisci rapidamente quelle sporche.
UI_EHR_Codex_wound_infection_Treatment: Disinfetta le ferite, usa una pomata antibiotica e passa agli antibiotici se l'infezione si diffonde.
UI_EHR_Codex_cellulitis_Cause: Infezione batterica cutanea che si diffonde dopo la chiusura inadeguata di una ferita. Una sutura grossolana comporta un alto rischio di cellulite infettiva.
UI_EHR_Codex_cellulitis_Symptoms: Pelle calda e arrossata, gonfiore, dolore locale, febbre, stanchezza, debolezza e resistenza ridotta. Lo stadio 4 non trattato può evolvere in sepsi.
UI_EHR_Codex_cellulitis_Prevention: Pulisci le ferite prima di suturare, usa materiale sterile ed evita suture grossolane quando possibile.
UI_EHR_Codex_cellulitis_Treatment: La pomata antibiotica può trattare i casi lievi. Antibiotici su prescrizione, ad ampio spettro, vegetali, endovenosi o vancomicina endovenosa trattano i casi più gravi. Antinfiammatori e antipiretici riducono solo i sintomi.
UI_EHR_Codex_sepsis_Cause: Infezione grave non trattata che raggiunge il sangue.
UI_EHR_Codex_sepsis_Symptoms: Febbre alta, debolezza estrema, confusione, rapido peggioramento e malattia sistemica potenzialmente fatale.
UI_EHR_Codex_sepsis_Prevention: Tratta le infezioni delle ferite e la cellulite infettiva prima che si diffondano.
UI_EHR_Codex_sepsis_Treatment: Antibiotici endovenosi e supporto medico intensivo. È un'emergenza.
UI_EHR_Codex_tetanus_Cause: Ferite profonde contaminate da puntura, lesioni da metallo arrugginito o gravi ferite sporche.
UI_EHR_Codex_tetanus_Symptoms: Rigidità della mandibola, spasmi muscolari, dolore, febbre e pericolosa disfunzione neuromuscolare.
UI_EHR_Codex_tetanus_Prevention: Pulisci rapidamente le ferite profonde e usa la profilassi antitetanica quando possibile.
UI_EHR_Codex_tetanus_Treatment: Miorilassanti per i sintomi; antitossina o immunoglobuline antitetaniche con una siringa per curare.
UI_EHR_Codex_hyperkeratotic_scabies_Caus: Esposizione prolungata a terra o erba contaminata. Il primo morso lascia una ferita simile a un graffio.
UI_EHR_Codex_hyperkeratotic_scabies_Symp: Prurito intenso, ferite ripetute da graffio, dolore nel punto del morso, febbre e pericoloso calo di salute negli stadi avanzati.
UI_EHR_Codex_hyperkeratotic_scabies_Prev: Evita di sostare a lungo su terra nuda o erba, copri la pelle esposta e mantieni pulite le ferite.
UI_EHR_Codex_hyperkeratotic_scabies_Trea: La permetrina topica è il trattamento principale. Anche le compresse antiparassitarie possono curarla, ma il ciclo è più lungo.
UI_EHR_Codex_concussion_Cause: Forte colpo alla testa dovuto a una caduta dall'alto o a un grave incidente stradale.
UI_EHR_Codex_concussion_Symptoms: Mal di testa, vertigini, vista offuscata, nausea e disorientamento che migliorano gradualmente.
UI_EHR_Codex_concussion_Prevention: Evita cadute dall'alto e incidenti gravi. Considera pericolosi i colpi alla testa anche se riesci ancora a camminare.
UI_EHR_Codex_concussion_Treatment: Nessuna cura diretta. Riposo e tempo sono il trattamento principale; i farmaci sintomatici possono agevolare il recupero.
UI_EHR_Codex_delirium_Cause: Stress estremo mantenuto al limite per molte ore.
UI_EHR_Codex_delirium_Symptoms: Allucinazioni uditive, discorsi irrazionali, distorsioni visive e comportamenti impulsivi pericolosi.
UI_EHR_Codex_delirium_Prevention: Riduci lo stress prima che rimanga al massimo a lungo.
UI_EHR_Codex_delirium_Treatment: Antipsicotici. Richiede un ciclo di 8 dosi in 4 giorni.
UI_EHR_Codex_ahtr_Duration: 2-4 giorni senza trattamento; può diventare fatale rapidamente.
UI_EHR_Codex_ahtr_Cause: Ricevere sangue incompatibile con il proprio organismo.
UI_EHR_Codex_ahtr_Symptoms: Dolore lombare, grave debolezza, nausea, febbre alta, emolisi, perdita di resistenza e pericoloso calo di salute.
UI_EHR_Codex_ahtr_Prevention: Usa sangue compatibile e verifica la compatibilità quando possibile.
UI_EHR_Codex_ahtr_Treatment: Liquidi endovenosi e furosemide sono i trattamenti principali. Antipiretici, compresse antinausea e antinfiammatori riducono i sintomi.
UI_EHR_Codex_knox_infection_Symptoms: Febbre, nausea, debolezza, pallore e infezione sistemica terminale.

UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_1_1: Hey hey. It's yours truly, Amelie. How's your morning, folks? Mine is awful... as usual.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_1_2: I hate waking up early... but here I am, doing it for you. Try to appreciate that before something eats me.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_1_3: Anyway... if your hands are covered in blood, maybe don't eat with them. Revolutionary advice, I know.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_1_4: Soap, clean water, a clean cloth. Use what you have, but clean your hands before touching food.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_1_5: Unless you enjoy sprinting across town while your guts perform a marching band routine. Best-case scenario, by the way.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_1_6: Yours truly, Amelie. See ya later.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_2_1: Mmhh... aaaaggghhmmmm... Hello, folks... Amelie here. Hope your sleep was as awful as mine.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_2_2: A tip for today. A wound that gets hotter, darker, or meaner by the hour is not being dramatic. It may be infected.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_2_3: Change dirty bandages early. Disinfect every wound, even if it looks like a small scratch.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_2_4: If it starts swelling, leaking, or throbbing like it has opinions, clean it before it wins the argument.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_2_5: Boiled water, disinfectant, alcohol wipes, whatever you have. Luxury medicine died with the power grid.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_2_6: Do not keep poking it with dirty fingers to check if it's still bad. Congratulations, now it's worse.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_2_7: Yours truly, Amelie. Try not to rot from a scratch. It would be embarrassing.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_3_1: Heeelloooouu! And a special greeting to whoever woke up half of March Ridge with a shotgun.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_3_2: He or she is probably dead by now. Yeah... most likely. Definitely. Anyway, advice for the rest of you.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_3_3: Corpse smell is not bravery training. Leave immediately.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_3_4: Fresh air is treatment. A proper mask is prevention.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_3_5: If you start feeling sick near a pile of bodies, do not stand there investigating like a curious raccoon.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_3_6: Move, breathe, cover your face. Congratulations, you have discovered the ancient art of not poisoning yourself.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_4_1: *noises*, *noises*... God damn, this thing is harder than using an ESU. Hello, by the way.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_4_2: Raw wild game is a parasite lottery. Cook it through, especially rat, boar, bear, fox, and anything you found already dead.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_4_3: If the center is still cold or pink, congratulations, it is not dinner yet.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_4_4: Yes, I know you're hungry. The worms in your stomach will be thrilled to hear your excuse.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_4_5: Boil it, roast it, burn it a little if you have to. Charcoal seasoning beats intestinal misery.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_4_6: Yours truly, Amelie. Try not to lose a fight against breakfast.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_5_1: Welcome to The Last Prescription! You know what I miss the most? Beaches... calm, breezy, and full of people who are probably dead now.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_5_2: But you know what I hate the most? A fucking heat! I hate it, hate it, hate it, ha... *noises*
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_5_3: Heat is more dangerous than you might think. It kills quietly. Shade, water, and rest are medical supplies when the temperature starts climbing.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_5_4: A hat buys time. It does not make you immortal. Stunning concept, I know.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_5_5: If you stop sweating, get dizzy, or feel your head cooking from the inside, move before you become sidewalk decor.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_5_6: Drink water before you feel desperate. Desperation is not a hydration strategy, despite what idiots keep proving.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_5_7: Yours truly, Amelie. Stay cool, stay shaded, and try not to burn to a crisp.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_6_1: *Gulp* *gulp*... aaah. Hello, my lovelies. What have you been doing? Staying healthy like my grandpa in his nineties?
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_6_2: Anyway, here's some advice. I know you love advice. Sometimes I wonder how some of you survived this long.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_6_3: Untreated water can look clean and still ruin you. Boil it when you can.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_6_4: If your gut turns violent after bad water, hydration becomes the treatment, not a luxury.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_6_5: Sip slowly, keep drinking, and do not trust a puddle just because it looks polite.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_6_6: Yours truly, Amelie Crowe. Remember: clear water can still betray you. Very relatable, honestly.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_7_1: A deep wound with glass inside is not just a cut. Remove the fragments, disinfect it, and keep watching it.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_7_2: If something is still buried in there, do not pretend your body will simply negotiate with it.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_7_3: Use clean tools, clean hands, and whatever disinfectant you can still find. Yes, clean. That word again.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_7_4: If the wound gets stiff, swollen, hot, or starts hurting more, congratulations, the problem has evolved.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_7_5: Have you ever heard of tetanus? It's kinda rare until it is yours.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_7_6: Yours truly, Amelie. Try not to lose to a shiny piece of glass or a nail, would ya?
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_8_1: What's up, survivors? Did you stock enough meds? If your answer is yes, you're wrong. It is never enough.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_8_2: Here's a little advice for those of you who like shiny, colorful pills a bit too much.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_8_3: Do not stack serious medication just because you're scared. A bigger dose is not a bigger cure.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_8_4: Follow the interval. Your liver and kidneys are already negotiating with the apocalypse.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_8_5: If the label says wait, then wait. I know, reading is hard. Dying from impatience is harder.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_8_6: Yours truly, Amelie. Take the medicine, not the whole damn pharmacy.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_9_1: Good morning, survivors. Quick question: how much blood do you think you need to keep functioning? Hint: more than 'whatever is currently leaking out.'
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_9_2: Blood is not decoration. It carries oxygen, heat, and everything your body needs to keep pretending it has a plan.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_9_3: Lose too much of it, and simple tasks become ambitious. Walking, thinking, standing... all very fancy hobbies now.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_9_4: If you're bleeding, stop the bleeding first. Bandage it, press it, and do not admire the color like an idiot.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_9_5: Dizziness, weakness, cold skin, and a racing heart are your body politely screaming that the tank is running low.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_9_6: Yours truly, Amelie. Keep your blood inside you. Revolutionary, I know.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_10_1: Hi, it's me again. Still not dead. Today's topic is corpses, mold, and your lungs. Charming, I know. Try not to swoon.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_10_2: Cadaveric aspergillosis does not care how tough you think you are. Breathing rot is still breathing rot.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_10_3: Old bodies, damp air, and closed spaces make a lovely little nursery for things you do not want inside your chest.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_10_4: If you start coughing, wheezing, or feeling weak after digging through corpse piles, maybe stop treating dead people like furniture.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_10_5: Fresh air, distance, and a proper mask are not optional luxuries. They are the difference between clever and stupid with symptoms.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_10_6: Yours truly, Amelie. If the dead are growing things, do not inhale the harvest.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_11_1: Hello, lads. Amelie in touch. Today's miracle of modern misery: the common cold. Yes, even the apocalypse kept the boring diseases.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_11_2: A runny nose and sore throat may not sound dramatic, but coughing through a stealth run is a beautiful way to become lunch.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_11_3: Rest when you can, stay warm, and drink clean water. Basic advice, somehow still too advanced for half of you.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_11_4: If you're sneezing into your hands, congratulations, you have invented portable contamination.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_11_5: Cover your mouth, wash your hands, and stop sharing bottles like civilization is still handing out second chances.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_11_6: Yours truly, Amelie. A cold probably won't kill you, but your stupid decisions might.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_12_1: Mhmhmm... Is it already 9?! Still better than waking up in my office after surgery...
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_12_2: Today we discuss what happens when your skull loses an argument to a big bonk, a fall, or a car crash.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_12_3: A concussion is not just 'getting your bell rung.' Your brain is soft, expensive, and currently living in a bone helmet with terrible suspension.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_12_4: If you feel dizzy, confused, nauseous, sleepy, or your vision starts doing creative little tricks, stop acting heroic and sit down.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_12_5: Do not sprint back into danger because you 'feel mostly fine.' Mostly fine is how idiots upgrade minor injuries into permanent problems.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_12_6: Rest, avoid bright lights when you can, and keep someone nearby if things get worse. Yes, supervision. Like a child, but louder.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_12_7: Yours truly, Amelie. Protect your head. You only get one brain, and frankly, some of you are already using it very lightly.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_13_1: Hello, everyone, and hello to the walking dead folks who might overhear. Today we talk about hyperkeratotic scabies. Yes, even your skin can decide to become a cursed little ecosystem.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_13_2: Thick, crusted, itching skin is not just bad luck or poor fashion. It can mean mites are throwing a family reunion on you.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_13_3: Do not scratch until you bleed and then act surprised when everything gets worse. That is not treatment, that is teamwork with the enemy.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_13_4: Wash clothes, bedding, and anything your skin keeps touching. If you ignore the fabric, congratulations, you made the problem portable.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_13_5: Topical treatment helps, but consistency matters. One lazy application and the little bastards may file a renewal request.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_13_6: Yours truly, Amelie. If your skin starts hosting tenants, evict them properly.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_14_1: The one and only Last Prescription, live again. Today we talk about hypothermia, also known as your body slowly losing a debate with the weather.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_14_2: Cold is not just uncomfortable. It steals your strength, slows your hands, fogs your head, and makes every mistake more expensive.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_14_3: Wet clothes make it worse. Wind makes it worse. Standing around pretending you're fine makes it worse, obviously.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_14_4: Get dry, get covered, get indoors, or get near a fire before your body starts shutting down the less important departments. Like judgment.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_14_5: Shivering is a warning, not background noise. If it stops while you're still freezing, that is not improvement. That is bad news wearing a hat.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_14_6: Yours truly, Amelie. Stay warm, stay dry, and do not let the weather kill you with paperwork-level boredom.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_15_1: Yours truly, Amelie, back online! Today we discuss the Knox Infection.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_15_2: If one of our undead neighbors bites you, then that's probably it. THE END. Not right away, though. No, no, no.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_15_3: Fever, panic, sickness, and that lovely sense of doom. I don't believe in God, but pray before examining the wound.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_15_4: Clean the wound anyway, bandage it anyway, keep moving anyway. Giving up early is still pathetic, even when the odds are insulting.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_15_5: And if you know you are turning, do the polite thing: step away from the group before you become everyone's problem with teeth.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_15_6: Yours truly, Amelie Crowe. If Knox gets you, try to be useful before you become educational. For the rest of us...
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_16_1: Another great day... right? Amelie here, with your favourite advice. Today we talk about pneumonia.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_16_2: A cough, fever, chest pain, and weakness are not just your body being dramatic. Your lungs may be filing a formal complaint.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_16_3: Cold, exhaustion, wet clothes, and sleeping like a raccoon in a ditch can all help turn a bad cough into something uglier.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_16_4: Rest when you can, stay warm, drink clean water, take antibiotics, and stop pretending you can outrun sickness with heroic stupidity.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_16_5: If every breath feels harder than it should, take it seriously. Air is one of those little luxuries people only respect when it stops cooperating.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_16_6: Yours truly, Amelie. Keep your lungs working. They are annoyingly important.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_17_1: Heloooo, still living! Yours truly is still here, well and breathing. Today we talk about sepsis.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_17_2: A dirty wound is bad. A dirty wound with fever, chills, confusion, weakness, or a racing heart is even worse.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_17_3: Sepsis does not politely wait for you to finish looting the pharmacy. It moves fast, because apparently even infections have better time management than you.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_17_4: Clean wounds early, change filthy bandages, and treat infections before they start making executive decisions for your entire bloodstream.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_17_5: If you feel suddenly worse after an infected cut, bite, or burn, stop pretending it is fine. Fine does not usually come with shaking and seeing stars.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_17_6: Yours truly, Amelie. Respect small infections before they promote themselves.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_18_1: What's up? You know, I would give everything for a granola bar right now. Anyway, today we talk about trichinosis.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_18_2: Wild game can carry parasites, especially pork, bear, boar, and whatever mystery meat you dragged out of the woods like a proud little goblin.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_18_3: If the center is still pink, cold, or suspiciously chewy, it is not rustic cuisine. It is a medical subplot waiting to happen.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_18_4: Cook it through. Not wave it near a fire. Actually cook it. Or you'll get unfriendly snake neighbors inside you. Hate snakes, by the way.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_18_5: Stomach pain, diarrhea, fever, weakness, and aching muscles after bad meat are not proof you are tough. They are proof dinner fought back.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_18_6: Yours truly, Amelie. Eat cooked food, not consequences.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_19_1: Hello, world! Or what's left of it. Amelie again with some advice for ya. Today we talk about body temperature.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_19_2: Too hot, too cold, too shaky, too sweaty... your body is not being poetic. It is warning you before the machinery starts failing.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_19_3: Fever can mean infection. Chills can mean trouble. Ignoring both because you are 'probably fine' is how the probably part disappears.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_19_4: Check yourself after wounds, bad food, dirty water, cold nights, and corpse-stinking rooms. Patterns matter, even if thinking hurts.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_19_5: Rest, hydrate, warm up, cool down, and treat the cause instead of just complaining at your own skin like it owes you money.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_19_6: Yours truly, Amelie. Respect the temperature, or enjoy being cooked, frozen, or medically interesting.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_20_1: Hello, survivors. Today we talk about stress, because apparently being hunted by the dead is bad for the nerves. Shocking, I know.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_20_2: Stress is not just whining with extra steps. It makes your hands worse, your sleep worse, your focus worse, and your decisions impressively stupid.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_20_3: Too much panic can turn a simple problem into a full circus act, starring you, a locked door, and ten dead neighbors.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_20_4: Breathe, rest, read something boring, smoke if you must, and stop sprinting through every problem like fear is a navigation system.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_20_5: If your mind keeps screaming, lower the noise around you. Darkness, hunger, pain, and exhaustion are all very talented little stress chefs.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_20_6: Yours truly, Amelie. Keep your head steady, or the apocalypse will use it as a chew toy.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_21_1: Amelie Crowe and The Last Prescription, online! Today we talk about literature, because apparently paper can still do something useful besides starting fires.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_21_2: Specialized medical books can teach you about diseases, symptoms, and treatments. Even during the apocalypse you still need to learn. First aid especially.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_21_3: If you find one, read it before using it as kindling. Your future self may appreciate knowing the difference between a cold and your lungs declaring independence.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_21_4: The more you understand, the faster you can spot trouble. Fever, rash, cough, infection... all less mysterious when you have opened a book once in your life.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_21_5: No, reading does not make you a genius surgeon like me. But it does make you slightly less dangerous to yourself, which is honestly progress.
UI_EHR_Radio_Tip_21_6: Yours truly, Amelie. Read the manual before your body becomes the tutorial.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_1_1: Good afternoon, survivors. This is Amelie Crowe, broadcasting at three sharp, because apparently punctuality survived the end of the world.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_1_2: If you are hearing this, congratulations. Your radio works, your ears work, and statistically speaking, that already puts you above average.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_1_3: I used to run a clinic before everything went beautifully, professionally insane.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_1_4: Now I run this little miracle of static, sarcasm, and medical disappointment.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_1_5: Every day, same hour. I talk, you listen, and maybe fewer of you die from stupid little things.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_1_6: Do not get sentimental. I am doing public service, not adopting strays.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_2_1: Good afternoon. Amelie Crowe here, still alive, still annoyed, still better prepared than most of you.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_2_2: I found a clinic supply closet this morning. Mostly empty, of course. Humanity fell, but apparently someone still had time to steal all the antibiotics.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_2_3: There were three boxes of gloves, half a bottle of disinfectant, and a motivational poster about teamwork.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_2_4: I took the gloves and left the poster. Even I have standards.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_2_5: Today's lesson: if you find medical supplies, sort them immediately. Panic hoarding is not inventory management.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_2_6: Write labels. Count doses. Keep the good stuff dry. There, I have improved your life. Try not to ruin it.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_3_1: Good afternoon, my beautifully doomed listeners. This is The Last Prescription, and I am still your least comforting voice.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_3_2: Someone passed near the station last night. I heard a car engine, then shouting, then nothing smart after that.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_3_3: If that was you, well... your driving had personality. Mostly the kind that gets people killed.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_3_4: I stayed inside, because I possess the rare survival trait called not running toward noise.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_3_5: There are fresh dead around the south fence now. Not many. Enough to be rude.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_3_6: I will clear them later. Or I will pretend I did and call it strategic containment.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_4_1: Good afternoon. Amelie here. The generator coughed twice before starting today, which is always charming.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_4_2: Machines have personalities after the world ends. This one is old, dramatic, and deeply committed to testing my patience.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_4_3: I patched a fuel line with tape, prayer, and professional resentment.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_4_4: If your equipment starts making new sounds, do not ignore it. New sounds are machines writing goodbye letters.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_4_5: Check your fuel, your oil, your wiring, and your exits before you settle anywhere.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_4_6: A shelter is only safe until one small part decides to become a problem.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_5_1: Good afternoon, survivors. Today I discovered that the roof leaks directly above my medical shelf.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_5_2: Fantastic design. Really inspired. Ten out of ten, would curse at architecture again.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_5_3: I saved most of the supplies. Lost some bandages, a few notes, and one very smug-looking box of painkillers.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_5_4: Water damage ruins medicine faster than zombies ruin neighborhood property value.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_5_5: Keep supplies off the floor, away from windows, and out of damp rooms.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_5_6: Yes, this sounds obvious. So does 'do not drink bleach', and yet here we are as a species.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_6_1: Good afternoon. This is Amelie Crowe, broadcasting from a room that smells like dust, fuel, and poor decisions.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_6_2: I found old patient files today. Names, dates, allergies, little notes from before everything became a meat grinder.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_6_3: Mrs. Vance hated penicillin. Mr. Ellroy lied about smoking. A kid named Jamie kept hiding stickers in the exam room.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_6_4: Funny how paper can make ghosts without needing a single corpse in the room.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_6_5: Keep records if you are traveling with others. Blood type, allergies, conditions, medications.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_6_6: Memory fails under stress. Paper, annoyingly, tends to be smarter.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_7_1: Good afternoon. One week of broadcasts. Look at us, building routine in the ruins. Disgusting. Almost hopeful.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_7_2: A man knocked on the outer door this morning. Said he needed help. Said his friend was sick.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_7_3: I asked how sick. He said bitten. Then he asked if I had a cure.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_7_4: I told him I had bad news, clean bandages, and no patience for fairy tales.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_7_5: He cried. I did not open the door.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_7_6: Call me cruel if you want. Cruel is still breathing.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_8_1: Good afternoon, listeners. The man from yesterday left before sunrise.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_8_2: He also left a backpack at the fence. Inside: canned beans, a cracked watch, and a note that said 'sorry'.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_8_3: For what, exactly? Existing? Asking? Surviving badly? People apologize for strange things at the end.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_8_4: I took the beans. I kept the note. Do not make that face, you would have taken the beans too.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_8_5: If you cannot help someone, at least be honest. False hope is just poison with softer packaging.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_8_6: And yes, I hate that sentence too.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_9_1: Good afternoon. Amelie here. Today's weather: grey, wet, and emotionally committed to making everything worse.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_9_2: The dead are gathering near the east road. Not a horde yet. More like a committee of unpleasant intentions.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_9_3: I watched them for twenty minutes. No pattern, no purpose, just hunger wearing old clothes.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_9_4: People used to ask me why I sounded cynical. Adorable question, really.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_9_5: If a route starts filling with dead, change the route before pride turns into a funeral.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_9_6: The map is not sacred. Your plan is not sacred. Staying alive is the only thing with seniority.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_10_1: Good afternoon, survivors. I had a visitor on the frequency today.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_10_2: Not a person, exactly. A burst of music, two words, then static. Could have been another station. Could have been ghosts with poor timing.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_10_3: The words were 'Crowe, answer.' That is my name, unfortunately, so now the day is interesting in the worst way.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_10_4: I tried replying. Nothing came back.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_10_5: If you hear voices on the radio, do not chase them blindly. Hope makes terrible navigation.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_10_6: But yes, before you ask, I will be listening again tonight. I am arrogant, not immune to curiosity.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_11_1: Good afternoon. Amelie Crowe, still here, still pretending this microphone is a social life.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_11_2: The voice returned last night. Male, tired, probably local. He knew my old clinic call sign.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_11_3: That means he is either someone from before, or someone reading things he should not have found.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_11_4: He said the hospital still has power in one wing. Then the signal died, because drama apparently survived too.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_11_5: A powered hospital is either a miracle or a beautifully lit death trap.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_11_6: I am not going today. See? Growth. Wisdom. Mild cowardice wearing a lab coat.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_12_1: Good afternoon. I said I was not going to the hospital. I lied. Character flaw. Very human of me.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_12_2: I only scouted the outer road. From a distance. With binoculars. Like a professional coward, which is the correct kind.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_12_3: There are lights in the upper windows. Real lights. Not reflections. Not lightning.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_12_4: There are also too many dead at the entrance, because of course paradise has a reception desk.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_12_5: Someone is in there, or something left the lights on.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_12_6: Either way, I came back before curiosity got expensive.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_13_1: Good afternoon. Today I reinforced the station door, because optimism is for people with backup generators.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_13_2: I moved the medicine cabinet, packed a field bag, and cleaned my old revolver.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_13_3: Relax. I am a doctor, not a hero. The revolver is for doors, locks, and extremely final conversations.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_13_4: The hospital signal returned at noon. Same voice. He said, 'We have vaccines.'
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_13_5: That is either the best news in Kentucky or the laziest bait I have ever heard.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_13_6: And yes, I am insulted that it might still work.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_14_1: Good afternoon, survivors. Two weeks. If you made it this far, you are either careful, lucky, or hiding in a bathroom with crackers.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_14_2: The hospital voice has a name now. Daniel Price. Former emergency technician. Annoyingly convincing.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_14_3: He described the third-floor surgery wing, the staff lounge, the broken elevator, even the vending machine that stole my quarters in May.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_14_4: So either Daniel is real, or the universe has developed a very specific sense of humor.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_14_5: He says there are four people with him. One feverish. One injured. One child.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_14_6: That last detail was rude. Emotional blackmail with training wheels.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_15_1: Good afternoon. I did not sleep much. The walls made noises. The roof made noises. My brain joined in because it hates teamwork but loves sabotage.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_15_2: I keep thinking about the kid at the hospital. Daniel said her name is Rose.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_15_3: Could be fake. Could be real. Could be a trap with pigtails and a cough.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_15_4: I hate this. I hate that I care. I hate that caring still works.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_15_5: Today's advice: protect your soft parts. Not just organs. The other ones.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_15_6: The world will use them as handles if you let it.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_16_1: Good afternoon. I went farther today. Not inside. Just close enough to see the ambulance bay.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_16_2: There are bodies piled near the doors. Old ones. New ones. Some wearing hospital gowns.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_16_3: No screaming. No gunshots. No visible movement in the lit windows.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_16_4: I found a white cloth tied to a parking sign. Fresh knot. Fresh fabric.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_16_6: I hate when mysteries start making eye contact.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_17_1: Good afternoon, survivors. This may be shorter than usual. I am packing.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_17_2: Yes, yes, make your judgmental little faces at the radio. I can feel them through the static.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_17_3: I am not moving permanently. I am going in, checking the hospital wing, and coming back before evening.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_17_4: Medical bag, water, mask, gloves, crowbar, flashlight, spare batteries. See? Preparation. The opposite of whatever most of you call planning.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_17_5: If I do not broadcast tomorrow, assume I am delayed before assuming I am dead.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_17_6: And if I am dead, try not to act surprised. It is unbecoming.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_18_1: Good afternoon. I am back. Barely. Do not clap. It will annoy me.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_18_2: The hospital has power, yes. It also has locked doors, blood trails, and a stairwell full of dead staff.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_18_3: Daniel is real. Rose is real. The others were real too, until recently.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_18_4: There are no vaccines. Not for Knox. Not for miracles. Just medicine, lies, and people trying to make fear sound scientific.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_18_5: Daniel said he lied because nobody comes for ordinary sickness anymore.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_18_6: The worst part is that he was right.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_19_1: Good afternoon. Rose is at the station now. Eight years old, fever down, attitude improving, currently judging my soup.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_19_2: Daniel did not come back with us.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_19_3: He held the stairwell long enough for us to leave, which is a heroic way of saying he made a decision I did not get to argue with.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_19_4: I hate heroes. They make survivors feel untidy.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_19_5: Rose asked if I am always mean. I told her only when awake.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_19_6: She said that sounds exhausting. Smart kid. Terrible taste in soup.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_20_1: Good afternoon, survivors. Rose is sleeping. The station is quiet, which means my thoughts are being obnoxiously loud.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_20_2: The hospital followed us. Not literally, calm down. But some dead drifted this way after the noise.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_20_3: I cleared three near the fence this morning. There are more in the trees.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_20_4: The generator is running rough again. Fuel is low. Food is lower. My tolerance for cheerful thinking is underground.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_20_5: I may need to move the broadcast equipment, or abandon it entirely.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_20_6: Before anyone gets dramatic, no, I have not decided. I am simply surrounded by bad options wearing different hats.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_21_1: Good afternoon. This is Amelie Crowe, broadcasting from The Last Prescription, possibly for the last time from this location.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_21_2: The dead reached the outer fence before dawn. Not a horde. Just enough to make staying here stupid.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_21_3: Rose asked if the radio people will miss us. I told her radio people are imaginary.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_21_4: Then she said, 'But you talk like they matter.'
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_21_6: We leave tonight. If the station goes silent, remember something useful I said and pretend it was your idea.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_22_1: Good afternoon, survivors. If this recording plays, then I either made it out, failed spectacularly, or forgot to turn off the loop. All equally possible.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_22_2: This is Amelie Crowe of The Last Prescription. Surgeon, broadcaster, professional disappointment, and apparently babysitter.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_22_3: The station is empty now. Supplies are gone. Notes are hidden under the loose floorboard near the desk. You are welcome.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_22_4: If you find this place, do not stay long. The fence will not hold, the generator is a liar, and the woods have been getting louder.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_22_5: Rose says I should end with something hopeful. Fine. Here: knowledge lasts longer than luck.
UI_EHR_Radio_Story_22_6: Yours truly, Amelie. Keep breathing, keep learning, and do not make me haunt you over something preventable.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_food_poisoning_Cause: Rotten food is the usual culprit. Burned or stale food can still do damage.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_food_poisoning_Symptom: Nausea, vomiting, thirst, hunger shifts, and endurance loss.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_food_poisoning_Treatme: Anti-nausea tablets and electrolytes help. Activated charcoal can shorten the course.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_gastroenteritis_Cause: Dirty or bloody hands before eating. That is enough.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_gastroenteritis_Sympto: Hard nausea, vomiting, dehydration, and a gut that will not negotiate.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_gastroenteritis_Treatm: Anti-diarrheal medication and electrolytes are relief. Antivirals handle the illness itself.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_trichinosis_Cause: Raw or undercooked wild game. Rats, boar, bear, fox, and similar meat are the danger zone.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_trichinosis_Symptoms: Muscle pain, fever, weakness, and in severe cases, lethal systemic damage.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_trichinosis_Treatment: Antiparasitic pills are the course. Muscle relaxants only ease the pain.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_dysentery_Cause: Contaminated water. Rivers, toilets, and unsafe containers are not medical fountains.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_dysentery_Symptoms: Severe dehydration, abdominal pain, vomiting, and blood loss in advanced stages.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_dysentery_Treatment: Oral hydration, IV fluids, and the right antibiotics. Anti-diarrheal medication buys control.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_toxin_poisoning_Cause: Poisonous berries or mushrooms. One bad bite can turn the whole day hostile.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_toxin_poisoning_Sympto: Nausea, blurred vision, weakness, feverish collapse, and dangerous health loss.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_toxin_poisoning_Treatm: Activated charcoal can suppress the worst of it if taken early.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_corpse_sickness_Cause: Standing too long near decomposing corpses, especially without fresh air.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_corpse_sickness_Sympto: Eye irritation, nausea, dizziness, and collapse at high exposure.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_corpse_sickness_Treatm: Fresh air first. Respiratory support can help after serious exposure.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_cadaveric_aspergillosi: Fungal spores from damp, cold, corpse-filled spaces.
Coughing, respiratory fatigue, fever, and worsening lung stress.
Antifungal medication, inhaler support, and getting away from the source.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_common_cold_Cause: Cold, wet exposure, or being soaked long enough for your body to lose the argument.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_common_cold_Symptoms: Sneezing, mild fever, fatigue, and respiratory irritation.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_common_cold_Treatment: Rest, warmth, fluids, and cold and flu tablets.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_pneumonia_Cause: Often follows a neglected respiratory infection.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_pneumonia_Symptoms: High fever, severe cough, chest pain, endurance collapse, and health loss.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_pneumonia_Treatment: Antibiotics, fever control, cough medication, and bronchodilator support.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_hypothermia_Cause: Core temperature falling too far after cold exposure.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_hypothermia_Symptoms: Shivering, slowed movement, confusion, collapse, and lethal body cooling.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_hypothermia_Treatment: Warm shelter, dry clothing, rest, and time away from the cold.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_heat_exhaustion_Cause: Working or standing too long in dangerous heat before true heat stroke begins.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_heat_exhaustion_Sympto: Weakness, overheating, thirst, dizziness, and rising heat exposure.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_heat_exhaustion_Treatm: Shade, water, rest, and cooling before it becomes heat stroke.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_heat_stroke_Cause: Extreme heat exposure after the body fails to cool itself.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_heat_stroke_Symptoms: Dangerous fever, confusion, collapse, thirst, and health drain.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_heat_stroke_Treatment: Immediate cooling. Ice packs or a cold bath can save a life.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_wound_infection_Cause: Dirty wounds, neglected bandages, and poor wound care.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_wound_infection_Sympto: Local pain, fever in serious stages, and progression toward systemic infection.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_wound_infection_Treatm: Antibiotic ointment early. Broad-spectrum antibiotics if it progresses.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_sepsis_Cause: An infection breaking containment and becoming a whole-body emergency.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_sepsis_Symptoms: Extreme weakness, fever, health drain, and rapid decline without treatment.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_sepsis_Treatment: Clinical antibiotics and aggressive supportive care. Do not wait.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_tetanus_Cause: Deep contaminated wounds, especially with embedded debris.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_tetanus_Symptoms: Muscle spasms, neck stiffness, trouble eating, fever, and lethal collapse.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_tetanus_Treatment: Tetanus antitoxin or immunoglobulin. Muscle relaxants only make symptoms bearable.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_ahtr_Symptoms: Lower back pain, nausea, high fever, endurance loss, and severe health drain.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_ahtr_Treatment: Stop the reaction with IV fluids and furosemide support.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_concussion_Cause: A serious head impact after a fall or crash.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_concussion_Symptoms: Headache, blurred vision, dizziness, nausea, and temporary health loss.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_concussion_Treatment: Rest and time. Do not pretend your skull has a spare.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_hyperkeratotic_scabies: Infestation after prolonged contact with soil or contaminated ground.
Itching, scratches, fever, spreading skin trauma, and severe health loss.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_delirium_Cause: Prolonged extreme stress breaking mental stability.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_delirium_Symptoms: Auditory hallucinations, disorganized speech, strange impulses, and visual distortion.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_delirium_Treatment: Antipsychotics and removing the stress source if you can.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_knox_infection_Cause: A bite or infected wound from the dead.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_knox_infection_Symptom: Fever, anxiety, nausea, and the final progression everyone fears.
UI_EHR_Radio_File_knox_infection_Treatme: There is no routine cure. Experimental therapy is rare and uncertain.
